Since GITHUB_TOKEN is not set in the environment variables and no credentials are available, it seems the private `@sw-code/*` packages are inaccessible. Let me check the GitHub package — I'll check whether the package might be public. A 401 on npm.pkg.github.com without authentication suggests that authentication is required. Let me verify whether the package is actually public (some GitHub packages are public and can be accessed without a token... actually, even for public GitHub packages, in the case of npm you need at least a valid token with the read:packages scope — in fact, for public packages, unauthenticated access to npm.pkg.github.com returns 401, but if you use any valid GitHub token, even an empty one, it can be used).

Let me check a few things:
1. Does the backend really need GitHub packages? In settings.gradle.kts, only the S3 maven repository and mavenCentral are shown — no GitHub maven. The README states that `common-conventions.gradle.kts` requires a GitHub token, but that file doesn't exist in this commit! The guide references `buildSrc/src/main/kotlin/io/swcode/menden/common-conventions.gradle.kts`, but the buildSrc directory only contains build.gradle.kts and settings.gradle.kts. In other words, the documentation is outdated — the current commit doesn't need a GitHub token for the backend.

2. As for the frontend (app, cms), the .npmrc file points the @sw-code scope to https://npm.pkg.github.com. Without a token, installation should fail with a 401/403 for those private packages.

Wait — but are those packages really private? Let me test: try `curl https://npm.pkg.github.com/@sw-code%2furbo-core` without a token → 401. That's the standard response. Some public packages on npm.pkg.github.com return 200 without authentication? No, GitHub always requires authentication for npm registry access, even for public packages.

Therefore, without a token, `pnpm install` in app/ and cms/ should fail on @sw-code packages. Let me check whether there are any other mirrors... The README of the repository is from gitlab.opencode.de — perhaps there's a mirror. Let me check the lockfile to see which registry the @sw-code packages are resolved from.

Let me check pnpm-lock.yaml.
